sn11.9:1.2: “Bhikkhus, once in the past a number of seers who were virtuous and of good character had settled down in leaf huts in a tract of forest.
sn11.9:1.3: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, and Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, approached those seers.
sn11.9:1.4: “Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, put on his boots, bound his sword on tightly, and, with a parasol borne aloft, entered the hermitage through the main gate; then, having turned his left side towards them, he walked past those seers who were virtuous and of good character.
sn11.9:1.5: But Sakka, lord of the devas, took off his boots, handed over his sword to others, lowered his parasol, and entered the hermitage through an ordinary gate; then he stood on the lee side, raising his joined hands in reverential salutation, paying homage to those seers who were virtuous and of good character.
sn11.9:1.6: “Then, bhikkhus, those seers addressed Sakka in verse:
sn11.9:2.1: “‘The odour of the seers long bound by their vows,
sn11.9:2.2: Emitted from their bodies, goes with the wind.
sn11.9:2.3: Turn away from here, O thousand-eyed god,
sn11.9:2.4: For the seers’ odour is foul, O deva-king.’
sn11.9:3.1:
Sakka:
“‘Let the odour of the seers long bound by their vows,
sn11.9:3.2: Emitted from their bodies, go with the wind;
sn11.9:3.3: We yearn for this odour, O venerable sirs,
sn11.9:3.4: As for a garland of flowers on the head.
sn11.9:3.5: The devas do not perceive it as repulsive.’”
